\section[pērakkuṭṭi]{\ml{പേരക്കുട്ടി} (pērakkuṭṭi) — a grandchild}

\label{lesson:ML-C125-grandchild}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for welcome, then the Malayalam for good wishes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പേരക്കുട്ടി}}
\textbf{\ml{പേരക്കുട്ടി}} (\emph{pērakkuṭṭi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a grandchild\textquotedblright{}. It ends in \textbf{\ml{കുട്ടി}} (\emph{kuṭṭi}), \textquotedblleft{}child\textquotedblright{}, which you already know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A known word inside a new one.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pērakkuṭṭi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pērakkuṭṭi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{pērakkuṭṭi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for welcome, then the Malayalam for good wishes, then say \emph{pērakkuṭṭi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പേരക്കുട്ടി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A grandchild\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bandhu]{\ml{ബന്ധു} (bandhu) — a relative}

\label{lesson:ML-C125-relative}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ബന്ധു}}
\textbf{\ml{ബന്ധു}} (\emph{bandhu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a relative\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ml{ബന്ധുക്കൾ}} (\emph{bandhukkaḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}relatives\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The word for everyone the family tree connects.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for good wishes, then the Malayalam for a grandchild, then say \emph{bandhu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[ayalkkār]{\ml{അയൽക്കാർ} (ayalkkār) — the neighbours}

\label{lesson:ML-C125-neighbours}

\textbf{\ml{അയൽക്കാർ}} (\emph{ayalkkār}) — \textquotedblleft{}the neighbours\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\ml{അയൽ}} (\emph{ayal}), \textquotedblleft{}next door\textquotedblright{}.

The people close to home.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a grandchild, then the Malayalam for a relative, then say \emph{ayalkkār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[marumakan]{\ml{മരുമകൻ} (marumakan) — a nephew; a son-in-law}

\label{lesson:ML-C125-nephew}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മരുമകൻ}}
\textbf{\ml{മരുമകൻ}} (\emph{marumakan}) — \textquotedblleft{}a nephew\textquotedblright{}, and also \textquotedblleft{}a son-in-law\textquotedblright{}. It contains \textbf{\ml{മകൻ}} (\emph{makan}), \textquotedblleft{}son\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Son, one step removed.
\end{grammarlens}
